description: Open, content-addressed admission-gate context over the AlgoVoi substrate (RFC 8785 JCS + SHA-256). guard_context_ref = "sha256:" + SHA-256(JCS({canon_version, type, guard_timestamp_ms, policy_ref, mandate_ref, passport_credential_ref})), pinning the exact policy, mandate, and passport the admission gate saw at an integer-millisecond moment, so the guard decision is reproducible offline. Each ref input is imported by hash; guard_timestamp_ms is an integer millisecond (Substrate Rule 2). Changing the moment, the policy, the mandate, or the passport diverges the guard_context_ref. Lite tier: no signature; the commercial Keystone Secure adds Falcon-1024 signing + CCC posture ingestion.
note_inputs: policy_ref / mandate_ref / passport_credential_ref are imported by hash. passport and mandate reuse the published spend_guardrail_lite_v1 subjects; policy_ref is a raw substrate-canonical policy reference (the guard sees policy_ref, not policy_bound_ref). guard_timestamp_ms is an integer-millisecond epoch value.

negatives.note: same policy + mandate + passport, but a different guard_timestamp_ms; the guard_context_ref diverges -> the context is bound to the moment the gate saw it
same moment + policy + mandate, but a different passport_credential_ref; the guard_context_ref diverges -> the context is bound to the passport in force at the gate

negatives.reason: guard_timestamp_ms must be an integer millisecond (Substrate Rule 2); a floating-point timestamp is rejected, not hashed
policy_ref must be a sha256: 64-hex reference; a malformed ref is rejected, not hashed

invariants.assert: guard_context_ref changes when only guard_timestamp_ms changes
invariants.reason: the admission context is bound to the moment in time; two gate evaluations at different instants are byte-distinct
Substrate Rule 2 -- epoch-millisecond integers hashed directly, no floating point
